# REGIME READ — 2026-09-25

## Changes Since Previous Read
- **Stage: 3 → 3 (unchanged), but one bearish trigger fired.** The 10Y closed at **5.162%** on 09-24 (+0.94%, snapshot). That is the second close in a row above 5.00%, after 5.114% on 09-23. The previous read listed this as a bearish (Stage 3 → 4) trigger, and it has fired. I am still holding at Stage 3. The reason is that Stage 4 is defined by VIX at 20–30 and rising, with breadth getting worse. VIX is 15.06 (09-25, yfinance) and falling, so it is 32.8% short of 20. The rate leg fired. The volatility leg did not follow. Read Stage 3 as the lowest-conviction Stage 3 possible, one volatility spike away from 4.
- **Total score: −5 → −5 (delta 0).** No lens changed its score. The mix is still 0 bullish, 3 bearish and 4 neutral.
- **Triggers from previous read:**
  - *Bullish — VIX below 15, 10Y below 5.00% and NDX above 30,000 (all three together):* **ARMED, and blocked by the 10Y.** VIX is at 15.06 and needs only −0.40%. NDX is at 30,478.86 and holds. The 10Y moved further away, to 5.162%, and needs about −3.1%.
  - *Bullish — TQQQ close above $86.35 (RALLY):* **ARMED.** TQQQ needs +9.89% from $78.58.
  - *Bearish — a second 10Y close at or above 5.00%:* **FIRED.** 5.162% on 09-24 ([TheStreet](https://www.thestreet.com/stock-market-today/stock-market-today-dow-jones-sp-500-nasdaq-updates-sept-24-2026) reports that yields hit a fresh high since 2007).
  - *Bearish — NDX closing below 30,000:* **DID NOT FIRE.** NDX needs −1.57%. That is almost unchanged from −1.54%.
  - *Bearish — VXN above 22:* **DID NOT FIRE, but it moved closer.** VXN is 21.24 (+2.31%, 09-24) and needs +3.58%. It needed +5.97% last read.
  - *Bearish — VIX above 20 and rising:* **DID NOT FIRE.** VIX needs +32.8%.
  - *Bearish — HY OAS through 3.25% with IG above 0.90%:* **DID NOT FIRE.** HY is at 2.73% (+5bp) and IG at 0.77% (flat), both 09-23 (FRED).
  - *Bearish — TQQQ closing below the $70.76 50DMA:* **DID NOT FIRE.** The 50DMA is now $70.84, and TQQQ needs −9.85% to reach it.
- **Notable lens flips:** none in score. Inside the lenses:
  - Dealer flow: MOVE rose again, to 104.58 (+9.57%). VIX eased to 15.06.
  - Positioning: TQQQ put/call fell back from 1.73 to 0.78. The one-day hedging burst faded.
  - Cross-asset: the Brent feed now shows 98.37 (−7.72%). That conflicts with press prints of about $105.7 (see data note).

## Regime Stage Tracker
- Current Stage: 3 — Neutral / choppy
- Stage Anchor: 2026-09-23/24. The 10Y set back-to-back closes above 5% (5.114%, then 5.162%), the highest levels since 2007. VIX broke back above 15 during this stretch.
- Position: Week 1 of an estimated 1–3. This is the second read in Stage 3.
- Confidence: Medium. Four lenses are neutral and three are bearish, with none bullish. The one fired bearish trigger has not been confirmed by volatility.
- Bullish trigger (-> next bullish stage): all three together:
  - VIX below 15 (−0.40%).
  - The 10Y back below 5.00% on a close (about −3.1%).
  - NDX holding above 30,000.
- Bearish trigger (-> next bearish stage): any one of these:
  - VIX above 20 (+32.8%) and rising.
  - VXN above 22 (+3.58%) together with NDX closing below 30,000 (−1.57%).
  - HY OAS through 3.25% with IG above 0.90%.
  - The 10Y extending above 5.25% while breadth stays under 35% of stocks above their 50-day average.

## Regime Verdict
The bond market is still the main driver of this tape. The 10Y has closed at 2007 highs twice in a row. The Nasdaq is flat within 1% of its record, and equity volatility has not repriced to match. I read this as a choppy, rate-sensitive Stage 3 that is closer to Stage 4 than the calm VIX suggests. Medium confidence.

**Data note:** WebSearch was available, so this is a full read with no confidence cap. Four items need care:
1. **The Brent figures conflict.**
   - The snapshot shows $98.37 (−7.72%, 09-25).
   - [The National](https://www.thenationalnews.com/business/energy/2026/09/25/oil-prices-waver-in-face-of-iran-war-truce-and-houthi-attacks/) reports Brent at **$105.7 (−0.88%) on Friday**, down from a $108 high the session before.
   - A one-day fall of about 7.7% has no matching headline. The feed probably rolled contracts again, as flagged last read. I copied the table verbatim, but I use about $105–108 for the analysis.
2. **The VIX value of 15.06 is dated 09-25.** That is probably an early print, not a session close. The engine's 09-24 close was 15.67 (VIX/VIX3M line).
3. **The Day Change figures reconcile this time.** AP has SPX at −1.90 pts, Nasdaq at +3.34 and DJI at −161.61 (−0.3%) ([ABC/AP](https://abcnews.com/Business/wireStory/major-us-stock-indexes-fared-thursday-9242026-136734081)), which matches the snapshot.
4. **Not retrieved:** AAII, CFTC COT, NAAIM, margin debt, ETF flows, Citi Economic Surprise, insiders and buybacks, Copper/Gold, transports, Bitcoin, and breadth after 09-22. I also did not check the outcome of the final days of Xi's visit.

## Diverging Signals
- **Bond volatility against equity volatility.** MOVE is at 104.58 and has jumped two days in a row. VIX eased to 15.06. The bond market is pricing real uncertainty that the stock options market is not. In past episodes, the gap has usually closed with VIX rising, but that is a tendency, not a rule.
- **Index level against participation.** NDX is 0.9% from its record. The Dow and R2K are 6–8% below theirs, and only about 30% of S&P stocks were above their 50-day average (09-22). A few mega-caps are holding the index up. The Oracle force-majeure headline hit exactly that group (ORCL fell about 4% on 09-24, [TheStreet](https://www.thestreet.com/stock-market-today/stock-market-today-dow-jones-sp-500-nasdaq-updates-sept-24-2026)).
- **Credit against rates.** HY at 2.73% and IG at 0.77% show no stress, even with the 10Y above 5.1%. So far this is an inflation and term-premium repricing, not a growth or credit scare. That difference is why Stage 4 has not been confirmed.

## TQQQ Read
- **Momentum: neutral.** RSI(14) cooled from 67.9 to **64.3** (09-24) over two small red days. The fund is no longer pressing on the 70 line (where a move is considered stretched). It is not oversold either. For a put seller, this means no mean-reversion tailwind in the premium.
- **Market structure: SIDEWAYS.**
  - RALLY fails: spot is 18.31% above the 4-week low of $66.42, and it needs more than 30% (the line is $86.35).
  - DOWNTURN fails on both legs: spot is only 2.94% below the 4-week high of $80.96, not 20%, and VXN is 21.24, below 25.
  - This is the twentieth consecutive SIDEWAYS read.
- **Trend: uptrend on both horizons.** Spot is 10.92% above the 50DMA and 25.5% above the 200DMA. The lower edge of the 5-day expected-move band ($71.52) sits about $0.68 above the 50DMA.
- **Volatility & premium environment: slightly better for the seller than last read.**
  - IV/HV (20d) rose from 1.11 to **1.15** (HV20 49.4%, daily plan 09-24). Options now cost about 15% more than the fund has actually been moving.
  - Quoted ATM IV rose from 55% to **57%**, and VXN rose to 21.24. That is still well below the ~3x-VXN estimate of 63.7%, so TQQQ's own options remain cheaper than the index-fear scaling implies.
  - SKEW is at 146, so crash protection remains expensive. The richer premium still sits further down the chain rather than at the money.
- **Put-selling context: CAUTIOUS.**
  - The rate leg of HOSTILE has now fully fired: two 10Y closes above 5.00%, the latest at 5.162%.
  - The other HOSTILE legs are not close. VXN would need to rise 17.7% to reach 25. Spot is 18.31% above the 4-week low. HY is at 2.73%, well below 3.25%.
  - For a put seller, the premium cushion improved a little. The underlying risk has not changed: the index is near its highs on narrow leadership, and the long-bond yield is setting direction. A rate-driven down day can arrive without a headline, and a 3x fund amplifies it.

  This is context only — no strikes, expiries, sizes, or trade calls.

## Forward Levels & Triggers
- Bullish trigger: the 10Y back below 5.00% on a close, VIX below 15 and NDX holding 30,000, which would return the regime to Stage 2. For TQQQ, a close above $86.35 flips the structure to RALLY.
- Bearish trigger: VIX above 20; VXN above 22 (+3.58%) together with NDX below 30,000 (−1.57%); or TQQQ closing below the $70.84 50DMA (−9.85%).
- Neutralizer: a signed US–Iran deal to reopen Hormuz would take pressure off oil and could pull yields lower. A breakdown in the talks, or more Houthi strikes on Saudi export terminals, would do the opposite. A hot NFP on Oct 2 would push the 10Y further above 5%.

## This Period's Catalysts
- **Sep 30 (Wed): quarter-end.** Index and fund rebalancing flows, into a month with big moves in yields and oil.
- **Oct 2 (Fri) 08:30 ET: NFP / jobs report (Sep data)** (bls.gov schedule, verified 2026-08-29). This is the first major data print since the 10Y broke 5%.
- **Ongoing: US–Iran talks in New York** on reopening Hormuz, alongside Houthi strikes on Saudi targets.
- **Ongoing: fallout from Oracle's force-majeure notice** on AI data-center capex.
- Other scheduled macro releases in this window (for example PCE) were not in the injected calendar and were not verified. I have not listed them.

## Expiry-Window Flag
- Catalysts inside the next 5 trading days: NFP on Oct 2. Oct 2 is the 5th session after today (Sep 28, 29, 30, Oct 1, 2).
- Window: EVENT-WINDOW

## Structural Calendar Flag (deterministic — always report)
- **Quad-witching:** the next one is Fri **Dec 18, 2026**, 84 calendar days away. It is not inside 2 sessions.
- **Quarter-end rebalance:** Wed **Sep 30, 2026**, 5 calendar days and 4 sessions (counting today) away. It is not inside 2 sessions yet. It moves inside the 2-session window on Monday's read.
- Net: neither falls inside 2 sessions today. Next week, quarter-end will be close. Expect heavier close-auction volume and some drift on Sep 30, just ahead of NFP.

## EVENT ALERT — Historical Playbook
- **NFP Oct 2, 2026 (in a regime of 10Y above 5% and bond volatility rising):** the closest comparable is the long-end selloff of autumn 2023. **These episodes come from background knowledge and were not re-verified with sources in this run.** Treat them as illustrative:
  - **NFP Oct 6, 2023:** payrolls came in well above forecast while the 10Y was near 4.8–4.9%. Yields spiked at the open and equities opened lower. Stocks then reversed to close higher (SPX about +1.2%), and VIX eased afterward.
  - **NFP Oct 4, 2024:** a strong beat pushed the 10Y back above 4%. Equities rallied on the "no recession" reading.

  In both cases the first move was in yields. Whether equities followed that move or faded it depended on whether credit stayed calm, which it does today (HY 2.73%). I could not retrieve reliable average move statistics for NFP days, and none are given here.
- **Net alert:** in a rate-led regime, NFP matters mainly through the 10Y. A hot print with the 10Y already at 5.16% is the scenario most likely to jolt VXN over 22 and NDX under 30,000 in one session. A soft print could fire the bullish rate leg (a 10Y close below 5.00%). The gap risk runs in both directions. The downside is amplified 3x in TQQQ, and the 5-day expected move of about ±9% already brackets the 50DMA. Descriptive only — no trade calls.
